identity.wheat: The catalogue says 'Wheat'; the profile uses durum wheat (USDA 'Wheat, durum'). Other wheat differs.
identity.lettuce: Catalogue name covers Bibb, Boston and romaine; the USDA record is cos/romaine only.
identity.mushrooms: Catalogue name says 'button, shiitake'; the USDA record is white (button) mushrooms only.
identity.nut-butter: Catalogue says 'Nut butter'; the USDA record is smooth peanut butter without salt. Almond and other nut butters differ.
identity.sourdough-bread: USDA has no sourdough-only record; the record is 'Bread, french or vienna (includes sourdough)'.
identity.mint: Catalogue 'Mint' uses the USDA spearmint record; peppermint is a separate profile.
identity.kefir: The USDA record is a branded product (Lifeway, lowfat, plain). Other kefir varies.
identity.tofu: Calcium depends on the setting agent; the record is firm tofu set with calcium sulfate.
identity.hummus: Commercial hummus; salt, oil and tahini vary by brand.
identity.salsa: Ready-to-serve salsa with salt; brands vary.
identity.granola: The USDA record is homemade granola; commercial products differ.
identity.shrimp: The USDA record 'may contain additives to retain moisture', which raises its sodium.
identity.red-snapper: Mixed-species USDA record; species differ in mercury.
identity.sea-bass: Mixed-species USDA record; species differ in mercury (the caution says so).
identity.canned-tuna: Light tuna in water; albacore (white) tuna differs in mercury.
identity.tuna: Same USDA record as canned light tuna; consider merging or distinguishing the two entries.
identity.squash: 'Winter squash, all varieties' average; varieties differ.
identity.white-potato: Baked flesh and skin; boiled or fried potato differs.

servingState.oat: Serving is dry rolled oats; a bowl of porridge has far fewer nutrients per gram.
servingState.wheat-flour: Serving is flour, not a baked food.
servingState.red-lentil: Serving is dry lentils (the text says a cooked portion has about a third of these amounts).
servingState.squid: USDA record is raw squid; it is eaten cooked, and cooking changes the values.

unusualValues.octopus: Vitamin B12 of 36 µg per 100 g (about 1,275% of the reference per serving) is the USDA figure; it is an estimated value (no data points). Check against a second source before publishing.
unusualValues.bagel: Vitamin E of 7.5 mg per 100 g (about 52% of the reference per serving) is the USDA figure from two data points; unusually high for a plain bagel.
unusualValues.granola: Vitamin E of 11.1 mg per 100 g is a USDA estimate (no data points).
unusualValues.almond-milk: Vitamin E (111%) comes from fortification (USDA 'Vitamin E, added'); fortification varies by brand.
unusualValues.olives: Iron of 6.3 mg per 100 g (one data point) is high for canned olives.
unusualValues.mint: Iron of 11.9 mg per 100 g (two data points) is high; fresh herbs are eaten in tiny amounts.
unusualValues.clam: USDA sodium for cooked clams is 1,200 mg per 100 g, probably reflecting the cooking medium. A serving shows about 1,020 mg.
unusualValues.crab: USDA sodium for cooked Alaska king crab is 1,070 mg per 100 g.
unusualValues.shrimp: USDA sodium is 947 mg per 100 g (moisture-retaining additives).
unusualValues.scallop: USDA sodium is 667 mg per 100 g for steamed scallops.

safetyNotResearched.white-rice: Arsenic in rice: only brown rice carries a (unsourced) catalogue caution. FDA guidance on rice and arsenic was not read for this project.
safetyNotResearched.rice-cakes: Arsenic in rice products: see white rice.
safetyNotResearched.rice-noodles: Arsenic in rice products: see white rice.
safetyNotResearched.chocolate: Caffeine and theobromine content is not stated, and no source was read.
safetyNotResearched.spirulina: The catalogue cautions (contamination, pregnancy and autoimmune conditions) have no recorded source.
safetyNotResearched.tuna: The catalogue mercury caution ('prefer light/skipjack') has no recorded source.
safetyNotResearched.asparagus: Vitamin K about 46 µg per serving, below the rule that adds the blood-thinner note (100 µg per 100 g); an editor may want it.
safetyNotResearched.fennel: Vitamin K about 55 µg per serving, below the rule that adds the blood-thinner note (100 µg per 100 g); an editor may want it.
safetyNotResearched.coconut-oil: No saturated-fat statement is made; an editor may decide whether one is needed.
safetyNotResearched.butter: No saturated-fat statement is made; an editor may decide whether one is needed.
safetyNotResearched.milk: Raw (unpasteurised) milk is not covered; the profile describes pasteurised milk.
safetyNotResearched.eggs: Raw or undercooked eggs are covered only by the cooking-temperature caution.
